document_candidates.title: NICARAGUAN ELECTIONS
document_candidates.repository: U.S. Department of State FOIA Library
document_candidates.action: The report directly addresses Nicaragua’s February 1990 election and U.S. diplomatic discussion of the transition, matching Volume XXIII’s 1989–1992 Central America scope. Cuba is a secondary cross-reference, not the placement basis.
document_candidates.reportingDateNote: Report and meeting date: March 2, 1990. The report discusses the February 25 Nicaraguan election and its aftermath; February 25 is not the telegram date.
document_candidates.copyCitation: U.S. Department of State, Embassy Santo Domingo, telegram 1990 SANTO 002261, “NICARAGUAN ELECTIONS,” 1990-03-02, FOIA Library, case M-2014-23169, document C09000012, source PDF, pp. 1–3.
document_candidates.summary: Ambassador Paul Taylor reports his March 2, 1990 meeting with President Joaquín Balaguer about Nicaragua’s election and the transition after Violeta Chamorro’s victory. They discuss regional democratic transitions and Cuba.
document_candidates.relevance: The report directly addresses Nicaragua’s February 1990 election and U.S. diplomatic discussion of the transition, matching Volume XXIII’s 1989–1992 Central America scope. Cuba is a secondary cross-reference, not the placement basis.
document_candidates.textStatus: Searchable embedded PDF text; not independently checked against the facsimile.
document_candidates.textNotice: Search text may contain source OCR or local OCR errors. Blank, redacted, illegible, non-English, and handwriting content may not be searchable. No text was inferred or reconstructed from redactions. Page numbers are physical PDF pages, not printed page labels.

       SUBJECT: NICARAGUAN ELECTIONS

          1. CONFIDENTIAL - ENTIRE TEXT.

          2.  I MET WITH PRESIDENT JOAQUIN BALAGUER MARCH 2 TO
      DISCUSS THE NICARAGUAN ELECTIONS AS INSTRUCTED BY THE
      REFTEL AND BEGAN BY COMMENTING THAT IT HAD BEEN A GOOD
     WEEK FOR DEMOCRACY IN THE HEMISPHERE WITH THE
      ELECTORAL RESULTS IN NICARAGUA. PRESIDENT BALAGUER
       REPLIED THAT IT HAD BEEN SURPRISINGLY GOOD WITH THE
      VICTORY OF MRS. CHAMORRO IN A PROCESS THAT WAS MORE
        CIVIL THAN MOST PEOPLE EXPECTED. THE SANDINISTAS
     SHOWED BY THEIR BEHAVIOR THAT THEY WOULD NOT FOLLOW
      THE ERRORS OF NORIEGA, I.E. THEY HAD NO CHOICE BUT TO
      RECOGNIZE THE WILL OF THE PEOPLE.  I ADDED THAT ALL
       CONFIDENTIAL

      DEMOCRATIC GOVERNMENTS AND PARTIES NOW HAD A
       RESPONSIBILITY TO USE THEIR INFLUENCE TO MAKE CERTAIN
      THAT THE TRANSITION WENT SMOOTHLY TO REFLECT THE
      POPULAR WILL IN NICARAGUA. AS A DEMOCRACY OF
       LONG-STANDING, THE DOMINICAN REPUBLIC HAD A PARTICULAR

UNCLASSIFIED U.S. Department of State Case No. M-2014-23169 Doc No. C05706272 Date: 11/22/2017

                                     MR-2014-23169    B-00001382109      "UNCLASSIFIED"       9/25/2026



      CENTRAL AMERICA,
       ESPECIALLY EL SALVADOR AND GUATEMALA, AND THE POSITIVE
      EFFECTS WOULD BE FELT THROUGHOUT THE HEMISPHERE.

          3. RAISING THE SUBJECT OF CUBA, PRESIDENT BALAGUER
      VOLUNTEERED THAT THE PEOPLE THERE MUST BE GETTING
       IMPATIENT AND THAT THE POSITION OF FIDEL CASTRO HAD
      BEEN GREATLY WEAKENED BY THE VOTE IN NICARAGUA. THE
      CUBAN PUBLIC HAD BEEN AWAKENED AND WAS EXPECTING
      CHANGE, MORE THAN AT ANY OTHER TIME IN THE LAST THIRTY
       YEARS. HE ADDED THAT CUBANS WERE TIRED OF THE REGIME
      UNDER WHICH THEY HAD HAD TO LIVE. HE THOUGHT THAT
      THERE WOULD HAVE TO BE SOME CHANGES.  I ASKED HOW HE
      THOUGHT CHANGE MIGHT COME, NOTING THAT THERE WAS
       LITTLE EVIDENCE OF ANY CHANGE IN THE ATTITUDE OF
      CASTRO HIMSELF. PRESIDENT BALAGUER RESPONDED THAT, IN
       FACT, CASTRO SEEMED TO BE MORE RIGID THAN EVER AS
      EVIDENCED IN HIS CONFRONTATION WITH GORBACHEV.
      NONETHELESS, PRESIDENT BALAGUER THOUGHT THERE WAS
      CONSIDERABLE UNREST BENEATH THE SURFACE IN CUBA AND
      THAT THIS PRESENTED A VERY CLEAR CHALLENGE TO THE
      CONTINUED ROLE OF FIDEL CASTRO.

       CONFIDENTIAL

       CONFIDENTIAL

      PAGE 03   SANTO 02261 022155Z

          4. PRESIDENT BALAGUER BROADENED THE SUBJECT TO
     COMMENT ON WHAT HE CALLED HIGHLY ENCOURAGING CHANGES
        IN EASTERN EUROPE, AND EVEN IN CHINA. HE SAID THAT
      THE EVOLUTION OF POLITICS IN EASTERN EUROPE HAD PROVED
      THAT NO COUNTRY WANTS TO LIVE IN SLAVERY. A RECENT
        VISIT BY THE PRC AMBASSADOR TO COLOMBIA (SANTO DOMINGO
        1817) CONVINCED HIM THAT THE CHINESE WANTED CLOSER
      COMMERCIAL RELATIONS AND TO MODERNIZE THEIR OWN
       SOCIETY, ALTHOUGH HE OFFERED NO CLEAR EVIDENCE OF
       POLITICAL LIBERALIZATION.

          5. SUMMARIZING HIS VIEWS, PRESIDENT BALAGUER
      COMMENTED THAT PRESIDENT BUSH HAD RECENTLY ACHIEVED
     TWO GREAT VICTORIES IN THE FORM OF NORIEGA'S OUSTER
     FROM PANAMA AND MRS. CHAMORRO'S WIN IN NICARAGUA. HE
      COMMENTED THAT AS A LEADER OF A "NORMAL" DEMOCRACY, HE
      GREATLY WELCOMED THESE DEMOCRATIC ADVANCES ELSEWHERE
        IN THE HEMISPHERE. AFTER WE DISCUSSED SOME OTHER
       TOPICS (REPORTED IN SEPTEL), PRESIDENT BALAGUER ASKED
      THAT I CONVEY TO PRESIDENT BUSH HIS WARM
      CONGRATULATIONS. TAYLOR
